"{x}{x}{r}, destroy this: Return TARGET AURA WITH COST X from your GRAVEYARD to your HAND." Nothing about this worked. The CHOOSE held options as raw effect dicts rather than {name, effects} blocks, so opt.get("effects") was empty and the option did nothing. Inside it, SELECT_FROM_REF read a ref "MYGRAVEYARD" that no effect sets. And the follow-up was PUT_REF_TOP ref "MYHAND" -- an effect that puts a ref on top of a DECK, over a second ref nothing sets, where the card returns the aura to HAND. The PAY_RESOURCES cost also named its amount under 'resources', which that cost does not read.

"Cost X" is an EQUALITY against the X paid, and needed a new condition. Writing it as CARD_COST_LTE plus CARD_COST_GTE over {"type":"X"} does not work: inside an object-target filter the CANDIDATE is passed as the card argument, so _resolve_amount reads x_paid off the card being TESTED -- always 0 -- rather than off the card that paid the X. CARD_COST_EQ reads the source through context.current_effect_source(), which the interpreter pushes for exactly this.
